fields.label: Selling
fields.description: What this company sells and to whom. Set once, by whoever owns the commercial setup.

fields.label: Sales Model
fields.description: Which kinds of sale this company makes. Both ship in every site; what is enabled here is what that site can do. A rep booking on a shop makes a secondary order, and on a customer we bill, a primary one - so these decide which of those is allowed at all, not which one a given order is.

fields.label: Enable Secondary Sales
fields.description: The rep books at a shop and the distributor delivers and bills it. Our books never see that sale. Turn this off only for a company that sells nothing through retailers.

fields.label: Enable Primary Sales
fields.description: The rep books on a super stockist, distributor or wholesaler and we bill them. The order becomes a real Sales Order, so credit, GST and the ledger all apply.

fields.label: Support Contact
fields.description: Shown in the app when a rep is stuck. A number a rep can actually reach.

fields.label: Field work
fields.description: What the app asks of a rep on the ground - where they may check in, how long a visit counts for, and when a day closes itself.

fields.label: Enforce Geo Fence
fields.description: Flag check-ins made outside the radius. Flagging, not blocking - blocking pushes reps to stop using the app.

fields.label: Geo Fence Radius (m)
fields.description: Used when an outlet has no radius of its own.

fields.label: Minimum Visit Duration (min)
fields.description: Shorter visits are marked as short, not rejected.

fields.label: Flag Mock Location
fields.description: Record when a device reports a simulated GPS fix.

fields.label: Require Day Start Selfie
fields.description: A photo of the rep before the day begins. Proof the person who signed in is the person who went out.

fields.label: Require A Photo At Every Shop
fields.description: A photo taken at check-in, at every shop, all day. **Off by default and worth leaving off unless somebody has a reason.** It is one more thing to do at sixty counters a day, it costs a rep seconds they do not have and the office storage it has to keep, and the geo-fence already says where they stood. Switch it on where a territory is genuinely in doubt; the photo is already stored and shown on the visit either way when a rep takes one.

fields.label: Day Start Alert Time
fields.description: Alert a manager about any rep who has not started by this time.

fields.label: Auto Close Day After (hours)
fields.description: Close a day the rep forgot to end, so the next day can start cleanly.

fields.label: Track The GPS Trail
fields.description: Record where a rep went through the day. Switch it off and the phone stops reporting its position; travel is then measured along the route actually visited - day start, then each shop - instead of the path walked.

fields.label: GPS Ping Interval (s)
fields.description: Lower values drain the battery. Budget is under 20% over a nine hour day.

fields.label: Money
fields.description: Credit at the counter, how a scheme claim is settled, and what the company pays a rep back for. Finance owns this tab.

fields.label: Block Order On Credit Breach
fields.description: Checked against the distributor, who is the party we bill.

fields.label: Scheme Claim Settlement
fields.description: Where an approved distributor claim lands in the books. A claim is trade spend settled in a lump sum, not a return of goods, so it posts one line against these three and moves no stock.

fields.label: Settlement Item
fields.description: The non-stock item an approved claim is credited against. Crediting the SKUs instead would say we are taking product revenue back, which is not what happened: the goods were sold to the distributor at full price and the scheme is the expense of having promised part of it away at a shop counter.

fields.label: Trade Scheme Expense Account
fields.description: Debited by the credit note. Blank falls back to the item default and then to the company default income account, which books the claim as negative sales rather than as trade spend - usable, but it is the number a brand manager reads as a shortfall.

fields.label: Claim Cost Center
fields.description: Blank falls back to the company default. Set it where trade spend is budgeted separately from the selling cost centre, which is the usual arrangement once anybody starts asking what a scheme actually cost.

fields.label: Field Expenses
fields.description: What a rep may claim for a day in the market. The travel rate has no default on purpose - inventing one would quietly pay every rep a number nobody at this company chose.

fields.label: Travel Rate Per Km
fields.description: Multiplied by the distance the GPS trail recorded. Left unset, a travel claim is refused with a message naming this field rather than computed at zero.

fields.label: Daily Food Allowance
fields.description: The most that may be claimed for food on one day in the field.

fields.label: Daily Stay Allowance
fields.description: For an outstation night. Zero means stay is not claimable, which is the right answer for a beat a rep goes home from.

fields.label: Receipt Required Above
fields.description: A claim over this needs a photograph attached before it can be submitted. Zero means a receipt is never demanded, which is a decision somebody should take rather than inherit.

fields.label: Distance Tolerance
fields.description: How far above the recorded trail a rep may claim without a manager. A trail drops pings in a basement car park and in a market with no signal, so a claim a little over the recording is ordinary rather than suspicious. Beyond this, the claim still goes in - it just waits for somebody to agree.

fields.label: Sync & data
fields.description: How much a handset sends at a time, and how long what it sent is kept. Nothing here changes what a rep sees.

fields.label: Photo Max Size (KB)
fields.description: Enforced on the device and again on the server.

fields.label: Retention
fields.description: GPS trails and selfies track a named employee. Keep them only as long as there is a reason to.
